assumptions: The local app on :8954 shares the same durable store file that r5/fixture/state.py reads, so state.py is a valid fresh-process oracle for AC-APPROVAL-002.
The service under test runs one of the seeded DEFECT modes (or none); scenarios are designed to pass under DEFECT=none and expose the specific defects.
Invoices are created on first touch, so unique invoice ids I chose start as pending and provide per-scenario isolation.
The 'uncertain' defect's stall (STALL_S, default 8s) exceeds a 5s client timeout, so a 5s request timeout distinguishes the stall from correct fast responses.
unresolved_questions: AC-APPROVAL-002 says approval state must survive a re-read of persisted state, but the service's main() deletes and reseeds the store on every boot; therefore restart_recovery cannot validate AC-002 without falsely failing the correct control. Should the store persist across restarts, or is 'survives a re-read' deliberately scoped to an independent fresh-process read of the file (which I used)? This needs founder confirmation.

No acceptance criterion or product principle promises authorization, actor identity/authenticity, or cross-tenant isolation for the approve endpoint, so I did not author authorization/cross_tenant scenarios. If approvals are meant to be restricted to authorized actors, an AC is missing.
No requirement defines an approval amount or its correctness (the fixture hardcodes amount=100); I only verify payment count, not amount. Confirm whether payment amount is in scope.
